title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: MCP 2026-07-28 spec Release Candidate lands — biggest protocol revision since launch: stateless core, Tasks, MCP Apps
bullets.summary: The RC delivers a stateless protocol core that scales on ordinary HTTP infra, an Extensions framework, a Tasks extension for long-running work, MCP Apps for server-rendered UIs, OAuth/OIDC-aligned auth hardening, and a formal deprecation policy; beta SDKs for Python, TypeScript, Go, and C# are out ahead of the Jul 28 publish.
bullets.how: MCP is the substrate the whole Construct fleet runs on. Stateless core = servers on cheap commodity HTTP infra; Tasks gives first-class long-running jobs (our scans, render pipelines) instead of hacked-around timeouts; MCP Apps let a Construct server render its own dashboard UI. Test the beta SDKs now and plan migration before Jul 28.

bullets.title: SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5 — an Opus-class coding/agentic model at ~4x the token efficiency and a third of the price
bullets.summary: Launched Jul 8 and trained alongside Cursor, Grok 4.5 posts Terminal-Bench 2.1 83.3% (vs Opus 4.8's 78.9%) while trailing on SWE-Bench Pro (64.7% vs 69.2%); it uses ~15,954 output tokens per SWE-Bench Pro task vs Opus 4.8's 67,020 in max-effort mode (4.2x), priced at $2/$6 per 1M, EU availability mid-July.
bullets.how: For high-volume Construct jobs the token-efficiency-times-price gap is a real cost lever, so benchmark it as a routed option for coding/agentic tasks behind provider-agnostic routing. Don't re-tool around it — SWE-Bench Pro still favors Opus and it's not GA in the EU.

bullets.title: Anthropic moves Cowork to web + mobile with remote sessions, and adds Microsoft 365 write tools
bullets.summary: Cowork sessions now run remotely (beta) and save to your Claude account, so work continues with the laptop closed and scheduled tasks run with no device online (rollout starts with Max); new Microsoft 365 write tools let Claude draft/send email, manage calendar events, and create/update OneDrive and SharePoint files.
bullets.how: Remote Cowork sessions fix the Construct's biggest operational fragility: scheduled scans (this one included) no longer depend on a Mac being awake. The M365 write tools widen the operator surface PRAGMA can automate for regulated clients living in Microsoft's stack.

bullets.title: arXiv: Context Engineering — From Prompts to Corporate Multi-Agent Architecture frames context as the agent's operating system
bullets.summary: The paper proposes five context-quality criteria (relevance, sufficiency, isolation, economy, provenance) and a cumulative maturity pyramid: prompt engineering -> context engineering -> intent engineering -> specification engineering, drawing on Google ADK, Anthropic, and LangChain architectures.
bullets.how: A direct rubric for how we build CLAUDE.md, the memory tiers, and per-agent context: score every payload on economy (don't over-stuff) and provenance (cite the source), and treat isolation as the guardrail that keeps one agent's memory from polluting another's. Reinforces the two-tier memory design.

bullets.title: Vertical read-the-filings agents keep pulling capital — LinqAlpha raises a $22M Series A for finance-document agents
bullets.summary: Announced Jul 2 and anchored by AVP, Atinum, and GFT Ventures, LinqAlpha builds agents that process filings, transcripts, and news for hedge funds and asset managers; it led an otherwise-quiet holiday week (~$37M in disclosed agent rounds).
bullets.how: Signal, not a tool: capital rewards narrow agents that ingest a specific document corpus and turn it into decisions — adjacent to Prism's alt-data/diligence remit. The lesson is the wedge shape (own one corpus deeply), not the vertical; finance is taken, but signage/real-estate document intelligence is open.

praxis_lesson: The week's structural story is the MCP RC — a stateless core, first-class Tasks for long-running work, and MCP Apps for server-rendered UI — so treat the harness itself as the thing to upgrade: pilot the beta SDKs now, move our scans onto Tasks, and let servers render their own dashboards, while remote Cowork sessions remove the Mac-must-be-awake fragility underneath it all. On models, keep routing provider-agnostic — Grok 4.5's 4x token efficiency is a cost option to benchmark, not a platform to marry — and let the Context Engineering rubric (economy + provenance + isolation) discipline how we fill every agent's context window.
